Go Deeper

  • Why 81? — The Story of the Canon How Ethiopia’s church came to guard the widest Bible on earth.
  • The Honest Page How ancient books survive, what our marks mean, and the three passages nobody could find.
  • Reading Paths Three guided trails: the hidden books in 14 days, meeting Jesus, and a path for the skeptic.
  • Sabbath Teachings One teaching every Sabbath, gathered from the week’s reading — a full year of them, kept in the archive.
  • Glossary The words of the wider canon, in plain English — starting with why Meqabyan is not Maccabees.
  • The 81 Books — One-Page Chart The whole canon on a single printable page.
  • The Music Room Old recordings kept whole — chant, an oud from 1926, and the oldest song in the world — each with its credits.
  • The Gallery Historic sacred art on four walls — Ethiopian Gospel illuminations, the oldest church paintings, illuminated Psalters, and the great engravers — each piece with its history and its keeper’s name.
  • Places of the Book The ancient ground itself — Lalibela’s rock-hewn churches, Axum, Sinai, Bethlehem, the cave of the Apocalypse — photographed, each place with its history and the chapters of the canon that walk it.

The Museum

The library has grown a museum — a churchseum, in the word coined for this place: the art the canon traveled with, the sounds it was sung and rung in, and the very ground it happened on. Three rooms, and everything in them old, real, and freely given.

  • The Gallery Historic sacred art on four walls — Ethiopian Gospel illuminations, the oldest church paintings, illuminated Psalters, and the great engravers.
  • The Music Room Old recordings kept whole — chant, the oldest song in the world, and the bells of twelve towers — each with its history and its credits.
  • Places of the Book The ancient places of the canon that still stand — rock-hewn Lalibela, the scroll cave at Qumran, the cave where John heard the Revelation — each photographed, with its story.
